Episode 258. The Predator of All Dimensions (19)
His heart pounded. In truth, it was more of a desperate hope than a reasoned guess.

Just in case, Jin repeatedly turned his head to survey his surroundings. The battlefield's time was still not flowing. Only he, who had begun to climb the stairs, and the pulsating flow of magic and chaos inside Laprarosa were moving.

Jin embraced Valeria. His cheeks became wet again. The Valeria from the other world must have spent countless agonizing days, just like the one in his arms. She must have forgotten, lost, and given up many things to create this situation.

"Valeria. When I first learned about the multiverse, I was going to tell you my secret. I... had died once. I died in Akin in the year 1808 and regressed to September 9th, 1780, the day I was born. But today, I think I'm crying more than on that day I became a baby again."
He was out of breath, so his words were slow, and he kept looking down.
The ground was distant. Normally, he wouldn't misstep, and even if he fell, he wouldn't die. But now, he could die at any moment.
Suddenly, fear crept over him. Of course, he wasn't afraid of death itself. He was afraid that everything could turn to nothing in an instant. For the first time, hope was shimmering close by.
"Hoo-uk, haaaa...!"
He had almost reached the top of the stairs. Jin looked up at the lower part of Laprarosa, shining as if it would flow down instead of the sky.

A dozen auxiliary entrances were open. Lucy's dragons carrying the wounded, people about to go out for ground support, enemies looking for a chance to infiltrate, and the Iello and magic knight units waiting to descend were scattered chaotically at the entrances and in the nearby sky.
Jin connected his stairs to the entrance that led deepest into the bridge and stepped inside. The non-combat crew members, frozen like statues, all had desperate faces.

"...I don't know exactly why I regressed. It must have something to do with Solderet... Did he know everything? Did he know it would turn out like this? I hope so. That in the end, after this terrible fight, there's a future where salvation is actually scheduled. And I'm just a pawn to make it happen."
A predetermined destiny.

Jin was a person who had reached the rank of Genesis Knight by transcending destiny countless times, and even before becoming a Genesis Knight, he had always thought that way. That a person's will, their fighting spirit, was stronger than destiny. That no transcendent being could dare to decide and toy with the fate of a person or the world as they pleased.
But now, for the first time, he was hoping it could be so. Rather than the entire dimension sinking into Kelliark's desire, that was better.
However, before a few seconds had passed, anger surged up.

"I must be really tired. I've been spouting such garbage. Solderet... Solderet revived me just to throw me into this filthy and cruel fate? After I fought so fiercely, after I created a force the likes of which the world has never seen, we're all being crushed by one Kelliark, and now I'm in a helpless state where I can't do anything without your help? Don't give me that shit!"
Holding onto the corridor wall to drag his heavy body along, Jin screamed in a fit of rage.
It was a resentment directed at Solderet, at the world.
And at himself.
"What are you doing dilly-dallying, you bastard? Let's go faster. Laprarosa is... big. We have to go faster."
It was a super-giant flying fortress. Climbing the stairs, getting inside, and passing through a few corridors was not all there was to it.
He wanted to lighten his body. But he couldn't abandon Valeria. Even if she was dead, he couldn't. Jin looked at his left arm, which had stopped moving for a while now.
A strange thought occurred to him. Why was he still carrying this around in this situation?
"Kuhp!"

He just grabbed it with his right hand and applied a little force, and the left arm snapped off like a rotten tree branch breaking. Chu-haaak...! A basinful of black blood poured out, and a strong wave of dizziness washed over him.

After grabbing hold of his senses and using sealing magic to stop the bleeding, his body felt noticeably lighter. Since he had no sensation, he didn't even feel pain; it felt like he had removed poison, not an arm. In fact, the magic of Kelliark remaining in that arm was no different from a potent poison. It was just that the battle had been so frantic that he hadn't even been able to be conscious of it.
"Hah, I was so lost in pathetic sentiments about destiny and what not that I only thought of this now. I think my head is a little clearer too."
Jin straightened his back and fixed his gaze forward. He felt like he could run. He ran down the corridor without even looking at his own blackened left arm that had fallen to the floor.
Along with his left arm, one of his worries had somewhat disappeared.
Inwardly, Jin had been concerned about what would happen after Ameris and Rokia finished their work. Since he was too weak to even walk, that would be the best moment for Rokia to backstab him.
But now, it felt like he could fight to some extent even if such a thing happened.

"No matter what happens, I will have the legacy. I will finish him, and I will go back. Even if it's just the remaining people, we'll go back and remember. Who was here today, what happened, who the people who were with us were."
The Authority of Regeneration.
As he started running again, Jin thought of the authority he had gained upon reaching the rank of Genesis Knight.

On this battlefield, it had ceased to be a special power only he possessed. From around the time Linpa fell, all the Coalition members had begun to resonate with the Authority of Regeneration, and a brilliantly shining wave had begun to rise across the entire battlefield.

-The deaths that lie on the path you walk will not be your responsibility. It could be said to be the responsibility of the being who made you that way. But when you reach the end of that path... I feel that perhaps you may not be crushed by so many deaths. There must be a reason why you gained the Authority of Regeneration as soon as you became a Genesis Knight.
Was it because of those words Ayula had left him?

From some point on, Jin had harbored a vague expectation for the Authority of Regeneration. Since then, whenever there was a major war, the Authority of Regeneration had always left its light on the battlefield, just as it had in the Holy Kingdom.
Could it be that the lights that rose over the dead with the Authority of Regeneration could one day resurrect them?

Even while fighting the war with the Demon Army, Jin had harbored such a vague hope. He had no choice but to. If he thought that the people who had fallen so tragically behind him, the comrades he couldn't save, would never return, he felt like he would go mad.
But the light of regeneration, which had never once been erased in any battle until now, had been covered by the red sea and had disappeared.
That light would not be able to revive anyone. Therefore, all Jin could do was to defeat the enemy, survive, and remember them.
To remember, to miss, to strive not to forget, and to love.

Far in the distance, the entrance to the bridge was visible. As he entered, he could see Luet, Pettel, and the crew members looking out beyond the bridge. Those fighting outside and those supporting inside all had the same desperate look in their eyes.

The workshop where the curse was being lifted was directly connected to the bridge. He could find it immediately, as the crew members who had been constantly coming and going to check the situation were frozen in place.

As he got closer to the workshop, the scenery changed drastically. Ice had shot up all over the corridor like frost. He didn't feel the cold. Jin ran, staring at Talaris's back at the end of the corridor. Now, the magic and chaotic energy were churning just beyond the door, right in front of him.
"Lady Talaris, I'm indebted to you like this until the very end. Looking back, I feel I've incurred too many debts in this world that I can never repay since I've returned. Hoo, hoo..."
Jin said that and leaned against the workshop door, pressing his ear close. It was as if a storm was trapped inside the workshop; the magic and chaotic energy were vibrating fiercely.
"Lady Ameris!"
Bang, bang! Even when he knocked on the door, he couldn't feel any particular sign from inside. Jin was about to knock again, then turned around and sat down.

"Lady Ameris and Rokia must not know that time has stopped for everyone but us, Lady Talaris. Well, they must have been that focused. They have to release the curse even one second faster. I shouldn't have disturbed them and just waited. I was a fool for a moment."
Jin adjusted the position of Valeria, tied to his body. It ended up looking as if he were holding a small child.
At that moment, his vision went black for an instant.
"...Heok!"
He had lost consciousness. Jin snapped his eyes open, gripped his sword, and looked around. He had only been unconscious for about two seconds, and nothing had happened.
Jin wiped his cold sweat and leaned his back against the wall again. The vibrations caused by Ameris and Rokia from behind the wall were transmitted.

"Thinking that Lady Talaris is next to me seems to have made me relax. But... Lady Talaris. May I close my eyes for a moment? I have to cut down Rokia if she gets any other ideas, and it seems there's still a little more time until the curse is lifted, and a fight could break out in the legacy at any time. I need to recover my stamina, even for a moment..."

His eyes closed. As he lowered his head, Valeria's cheek touched his face. It was a cold and hard cheek with no warmth left, but Jin thought it was warm and fell asleep. There was no illusion of finding comfort. It was just what he thought.
"Jin!? Jin! When did you get here? Are you conscious? Look at me, your arm, why are you here in that state...! Priest! Call a priest!"
He opened his eyes again a minute later.
The frozen world was moving again. Talaris was shouting with a face and voice that had aged drastically.
"This child, is this Valeria? Get a grip! No, her breath... hah, quickly...!"
"Lady Talaris."
Jin calmly grabbed Talaris's arm, which was placed on his shoulder. Talaris stopped talking and met his eyes.
"Lady Talaris. The curse, is it all lifted?"
Talaris had also just opened her eyes, having been concentrating on the seal all this time. Since she too had just woken up, she didn't know the situation of the past twelve hours.
However, Talaris thought. That for Jin, who had lost his left arm on top of severe internal injuries, to be here with a dead Valeria, there must be a good reason.
"...Yes, it just finished. The magic and chaotic energy completely stopped moving. That's why I released the seal."
Clunk, chiiii...
The workshop door opened. Steam, created as the magic and chaotic energy were neutralized, poured out, and the figures of Ameris and Rokia were appearing.
